title: Run-lifetime exact-key adaptive representation registry

motivation.F_AHL30: A fixed non-evicting 32-entry cache causes thousands of repeated table builds when direct reuse exceeds capacity.
motivation.F_AHL31: Observed raw adaptive-table payload averages about 4.64 kB and projects to about 46-55 MB for 10000 unique representations; mean one-time build cost is about 1.25 ms.
motivation.F_AHL28C: Provider-local same-key memoization is retained after passing the frozen paired timing gate.

question: Can the shared representation store become a bounded run-lifetime exact-key registry that avoids repeated over-capacity builds without introducing linear-scan lookup overhead or a correctness limit?

candidate_policy.lookup: fingerprint-indexed open addressing with full exact-key equality on candidate slots
candidate_policy.growth: double slot count when insertion would exceed 70 percent load
candidate_policy.maximum_raw_table_payload_basis: approximately 90 MB using the F-AHL31 observed maximum payload projection
candidate_policy.over_maximum_behavior: build a valid caller-owned uncached representation and return success
candidate_policy.correctness: registry capacity is never a correctness limit

qualification.collision_safety: forced fingerprint-collision tests must return exact matching representations only
qualification.over_capacity_correctness: requests above maximum registry capacity must succeed uncached
qualification.reuse: 64, 256 and 1024 unique cyclic workloads must build each unique exact key at most once while registry capacity is available
qualification.lookup_scaling: warm exact-key lookup CPU must not grow linearly with registry entry count
qualification.hydraulic_semantics: no representation, dry-tail, near-saturation or solver gate changes
